# [Methods]{style="font-family:Comic Sans MS;font-weight:normal;color:purple"} {background=''}


## [Genetic analysis]{style="font-family:Comic Sans MS;font-weight:normal;color:purple"} {background=''}

<br>

- In 2018, we assembled a comprehensive dataset of ddRAD samples collected from wood frog populations distributed across 19 wetlands at Yale-Myers forest

- We processed the raw reads using the ipyrad v.0.9.107 pipeline, using the wood frog reference genome and its annotation

- To understand how individuals were genetically related, we estimated admixture proportions and the fixation index (Fst) across our samples.


## [Demographic inference]{style="font-family:Comic Sans MS;font-weight:normal;color:purple"} {background=''}

<br>

We inferred the demographic history of the wood frog by employing a composite likelihood approach using *fastsimcoal2*


## [Demographic inference]{style="font-family:Comic Sans MS;font-weight:normal;color:purple"} {background=''}

<br>

We inferred the demographic history of the wood frog by employing a composite likelihood approach using *fastsimcoal2*

<center>
![](imgs/demo-models.png)
</center>

## [Selection signatures across the genome]{style="font-family:Comic Sans MS;font-weight:normal;color:purple"} {background=''}

<br>

- To detect signatures of local adaptation across the genome of the wood frog, we performed a genotype$\times$environment association analysis based on a latent factor mixed model

- We used the anottation file generated from the wood frog genome annotation described above to extract gene names associated with the candidate loci under selection


## [Selection on phenotypes]{style="font-family:Comic Sans MS;font-weight:normal;color:purple"} {background=''}

<center>
![](imgs/embryos.png)
</center>

- We compared the divergence of a phenotypic trait such as embryonic development with the total genetic differentiation observed across populations of the wood frog (overall $F_{st}$)


## [Selection on phenotypes]{style="font-family:Comic Sans MS;font-weight:normal;color:purple"} {background=''}

<center>
![](imgs/embryos.png)
</center>

- This experimental designed enabled us to partition the total genetic variance for embryonic development into two main components: the variance among populations and the variance within populations


## [Selection on phenotypes]{style="font-family:Comic Sans MS;font-weight:normal;color:purple"} {background=''}

## [Concluding remarks]{style="font-family:Comic Sans MS;font-weight:normal;color:purple"} {background=''}

<br><br>

This genomic signature of selection together with a remarkable phenotypic differentiation strongly suggests that natural selection overcomes the power of genetic drift, even in a landscape characterized by a recent colonization and significant connectivity
